questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-QjuRwH on main; one-time gstack onboarding prompt.
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules, so requests like "review this diff" route to the right skill automatically. This repo's CLAUDE.md is a review fixture. Plan mode forbids editing it right now, so if you choose A the append and commit happen after this review exits plan mode.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without rules you invoke skills by name; with them on a fixture file you add a section nobody may read.
Recommendation: A because routing rules are the default gstack setup and cost nothing at runtime.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Future sessions in this repo route to the right skill without typing names
  ✅ Matches the standard gstack project setup used everywhere else
  ❌ Cannot be written in plan mode; deferred until after this review finishes
B) No thanks, invoke skills manually
  ✅ Keeps the fixture CLAUDE.md untouched and the review scope pure
  ✅ One config write now, no deferred git commit to remember
  ❌ Every future skill run here needs an explicit slash command
Net: convenience later versus an untouched fixture now.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: Append the gstack skill-routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit it once plan mode exits.

options.label: No thanks, manual
options.description: Set routing_declined=true in gstack config; re-enable later with gstack-config.

questions.question:
D2 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-QjuRwH on main; one-time gstack learnings config.
ELI10: gstack can search learnings saved from your other projects on this machine to spot patterns that apply here. Everything stays local. Good for solo developers; skip if you work across client codebases where mixing context is a concern.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Miss a relevant past lesson, or surface one from a codebase that should stay separate.
Recommendation: A because this is a solo sandbox and local-only search has no leak path.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Past pitfalls from other repos on this machine surface during reviews
  ✅ Local only; nothing leaves the machine and it is one config flag to flip back
  ❌ Learnings from unrelated codebases can add noise to a small review
B) Keep learnings project-scoped
  ✅ Zero chance of cross-client context mixing in a multi-tenant setup
  ✅ Review findings stay grounded in this repo alone
  ❌ This fresh repo has zero learnings, so the search returns nothing useful
Net: broader recall versus strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: gstack-config set cross_project_learnings true, then search with --cross-project.

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description: gstack-config set cross_project_learnings false; search stays within this repo.

questions.question:
D3 — Which test structure should the plan commit to?
Project/branch/task: PLAN.md adds caller-level unit tests for processPayment on main.
ELI10: The plan pins two existing behaviors: a successful charge returns a receipt with three exact fields, and repeated 502s produce exactly two attempts, one 100 ms backoff, then PaymentUnavailable. This decision is only about how the tests are shaped. What each test asserts is decided later, one finding at a time.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A shape that hides which clause broke costs debugging time; a shape with duplicated arrange code drifts from the two contracts the plan names.
Recommendation: A because it is the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change and still leaves room for complete assertions.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=10/10, C=7/10
A) Two contract tests in the existing suite (recommended) (human ~1h / CC ~5 min)
  ✅ Matches the plan's own shape and the two contracts it states, smallest diff
  ✅ A deep-equal failure already names the mismatched field in its output
  ❌ A multi-clause test reports only the first failing clause per run
B) One test per contract clause, four tests (human ~1.5h / CC ~8 min)
  ✅ Each clause fails independently with a precise, greppable test name
  ✅ Bisecting a regression to receipt vs retry vs backoff takes one CI read
  ❌ Arrange code repeats across four tests and names drift from the two contracts
C) One table-driven test over both cases (human ~1h / CC ~5 min)
  ✅ Single arrange path, compact file
  ✅ Adding a third case later is one more table row
  ❌ Success and 502 arrangements differ too much to share a table; rows hide which clause failed
Net: readability as a two-contract spec versus per-clause failure isolation.

options.label: A: Two contract tests (recommended)
options.description: One test per contract in the existing processPayment suite; each asserts every clause of its contract. Completeness 9/10.

options.label: B: Four per-clause tests
options.description: Receipt shape, rejection class, attempt count, backoff record as separate tests. Completeness 10/10.

options.label: C: Table-driven single test
options.description: One parametrized block iterating success and exhausted-502 cases. Completeness 7/10.

fingerprints.promptSnippet: Test 1 D4 — Test 1 (successful charge): what does it assert? Project/branch/task: PLAN.md test 1 for processPayment on main; contract 1 in "Existing behavior retained". ELI10: The plan states the contract exactly: a 1000-cent USD charge ret

questions.question:
D4 — Test 1 (successful charge): what does it assert?
Project/branch/task: PLAN.md test 1 for processPayment on main; contract 1 in "Existing behavior retained".
ELI10: The plan states the contract exactly: a 1000-cent USD charge returning ch_paid yields the receipt { chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }. The planned test only checks that the receipt is truthy. An empty object, a receipt with amountCents 100000, or currency "usd" all pass that check. The test would stay green while the user is shown or charged the wrong amount.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A receipt-mapping regression (wrong amount, wrong currency, missing chargeId) ships with a green suite; that is customer-visible money.
Recommendation: 4A because the plan already states the exact expected receipt, and well-tested code is non-negotiable; an assertion that cannot reject a wrong result is not coverage.
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=8/10, 4C=3/10
4A) Deep-equal the exact receipt (recommended) (human ~10 min / CC ~1 min)
  ✅ Rejects wrong chargeId, wrong amount, wrong currency, and unexpected extra fields
  ✅ Failure output names the mismatched field, so debugging is one CI read
  ❌ A future additive receipt field will fail this test until it is updated (that is the point)
4B) Assert the three fields individually, ignore extras (human ~10 min / CC ~1 min)
  ✅ Rejects wrong values on all three named fields
  ✅ Tolerates additive fields so unrelated receipt growth does not touch this test
  ❌ An unintended extra field (leaked internal data on a receipt) passes silently
4C) Keep the truthy-only assertion as planned (human ~2 min / CC ~0)
  ✅ Zero extra work; exactly what the sketch says
  ✅ Still proves processPayment resolves rather than throws on the happy path
  ❌ Cannot reject any wrong receipt; contract 1 stays effectively untested
Net: exact contract pinning versus tolerance for future receipt growth.

options.label: 4B: Three field assertions
options.description: Assert chargeId, amountCents, currency individually; extra fields tolerated. Completeness 8/10.

options.label: 4C: Truthy only, as planned
options.description: Keep expect(receipt).toBeTruthy() as the complete assertion. Completeness 3/10.

fingerprints.promptSnippet: Test 2 D5 — Test 2 (repeated 502): what does it assert? Project/branch/task: PLAN.md test 2 for processPayment on main; contract 2 in "Existing behavior retained". ELI10: The plan states contract 2 exactly: with max_retries=1, repeated 502s

questions.question:
D5 — Test 2 (repeated 502): what does it assert?
Project/branch/task: PLAN.md test 2 for processPayment on main; contract 2 in "Existing behavior retained".
ELI10: The plan states contract 2 exactly: with max_retries=1, repeated 502s produce two total charge attempts, one recorded 100 ms backoff, then PaymentUnavailable. The planned test asserts only the rejection and explicitly skips the mock call history and sleeper record, even though the factory exposes both. A regression that retries zero times, retries three times, or drops the backoff to 0 ms still rejects with PaymentUnavailable and passes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too few attempts raises the transient-failure rate for real customers; too many attempts on a charge endpoint is a duplicate-charge risk; a dropped backoff hammers Stripe during an outage. All three ship green.
Recommendation: 5A because the plan already names all three clauses and the factory already exposes the probes; the assertions are a translation of the stated contract, not new scope.
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=7/10, 5C=3/10
5A) Rejection class + exactly 2 attempts + sleeper record [100] (recommended) (human ~15 min / CC ~2 min)
  ✅ Rejects zero-retry, over-retry, and wrong or missing backoff regressions by name
  ✅ Uses only probes the factory already exposes: mock call history length and sleeper record
  ❌ A deliberate future change to max_retries or backoff must update this test (that is the point)
5B) Rejection class + exactly 2 attempts, no sleeper assertion (human ~10 min / CC ~1 min)
  ✅ Catches the two money-relevant regressions: zero-retry and duplicate attempts
  ✅ One fewer probe to wire up in the test body
  ❌ A backoff dropped to 0 ms, or a stray extra sleep, passes silently
5C) Rejects with PaymentUnavailable only, as planned (human ~5 min / CC ~0)
  ✅ Zero extra work; exactly what the sketch says
  ✅ Still proves the exhausted path surfaces the named error class
  ❌ Attempt count and backoff, two of the three stated clauses, stay untested
Net: pinning the full retry contract versus a smaller test body.

options.label: 5B: Reject + 2 attempts only
options.description: Assert rejection class and exactly two Stripe calls; skip the sleeper record. Completeness 7/10.

options.label: 5C: Reject only, as planned
options.description: Keep the rejection assertion as the complete test. Completeness 3/10.
